clue.text: Get off for a match

blocks.note: first meaning: step down from a bus or train
second meaning, read as two words: a match is something that gives you a light

explanation.surface: Someone climbs off a bus to go and play in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as A LIGHT: 'Got a light?' is a request for a match.
explanation.definitionFit: To alight is to disembark from a vehicle, while a struck match provides fire for a cigarette.

clue.text: Swimming pool with nothing under cover

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece placed under another simply follows it

blocks.note: a lid is a cover for a pot or box
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A swimming pool left completely open to the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue mentions nothing before cover, but in this down entry the nothing sits beneath, so it comes second.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public open-air swimming pool, a word common in Britain.

clue.text: A charity worth fighting for

blocks.note: first meaning: an organisation or appeal that raises money for those in need
second meaning: a principle that deserves to be defended

explanation.surface: Praise for a charitable organisation as something deserving support.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a deserving charity appeal and any aim that justifies struggle on its behalf.

clue.text: Coaches coaches

blocks.note: first meaning, a verb: instructs or tutors someone
second meaning, a noun: railway carriages, which strung together make up these

explanation.walkthrough: The same word twice, once as a verb and once as a plural noun; the second is defined loosely, since railway carriages joined up form the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To train someone is to teach them, and trains are made up of linked railway carriages.

clue.text: Growth of conciliation rejected by workers - a bad sign

indicators.note: something rejected is turned back, so these letters are read the other way round

blocks.note: the olive tree grows the branch held out as a symbol of peace and conciliation
men are workers, as in a firm's men

explanation.surface: Peace talks are thrown out by the workforce, an ominous development.
explanation.walkthrough: The olive branch is the traditional symbol of peace offered to an opponent, so the olive tree is the growth that stands for conciliation.
explanation.definitionFit: An evil omen is a portent of misfortune, something seen as foretelling trouble.

clue.text: Current account

blocks.note: surface reading: an everyday bank account
setter's reading: a bill charging for the electric current supplied to a home

explanation.walkthrough: A current account is a British name for a checking account; here current means the flow of power and account means a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: The utility company sends a bill for the electrical power a household has consumed.

clue.text: It may be put on disc

definitions.text: It may be put on disc

blocks.clueFragment: It may be put on disc
blocks.note: surface reading: something recorded on a compact disc

blocks.clueFragment: It may be put on disc
blocks.note: setter's reading: the personal details engraved on a soldier's or pet's metal tag

explanation.surface: Something that might be recorded onto a CD.
explanation.walkthrough: The disc is not a record but an identity disc, the metal tag worn by service personnel or put on a pet's collar.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog tag records who someone is, so their personal details are stamped on it.

clue.text: Gold blend tea in spout

indicators.note: a blend mixes things together, so the following word's letters are stirred up

blocks.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
taken as written, to be mixed

explanation.surface: A golden blend of tea poured through a teapot's spout.
explanation.walkthrough: Spout looks like part of the teapot, but it is a verb meaning to hold forth.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to make a pompous speech, which is what spouting off means.

clue.text: Academic sinecures?

blocks.note: surface reading: university posts with little real work attached
setter's reading: comfortable armchairs, since a chair is also a professorship and these are undemanding ones

explanation.walkthrough: A chair is a professor's post, and a sinecure is an easy job; the answer is really comfortable furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Armchairs for relaxing are restful seats, while the pun reads them as undemanding professorships.

clue.text: He should know how to press a suit

definitions.text: He should know how to press a suit

blocks.clueFragment: He should know how to press a suit
blocks.note: surface reading: a tailor or valet who irons clothing

blocks.clueFragment: He should know how to press a suit
blocks.note: setter's reading: a lawyer who pursues a lawsuit in court

explanation.surface: A man ought to be able to iron his own jacket and trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: To press a suit is to push a legal case, not to iron clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrister or lawyer pleads cases in court on behalf of a client.

clue.text: Slip by the Spanish church feature

blocks.note: el is Spanish for the
an apse is the rounded end of a church

explanation.surface: Someone slips past a Spanish church's architecture.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that elapses passes, so it slips by unnoticed.

clue.text: What an MP stands for

blocks.note: surface reading: the principles a Member of Parliament believes in
setter's reading: the electoral district a candidate stands for at an election

explanation.surface: Asking what values a politician represents.
explanation.walkthrough: An MP is a British Member of Parliament, and to stand for a seat means to run for election there.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliamentary district elects one member, whom it then sends to Westminster.

clue.text: Main part of a book taken by travellers

definitions.note: a description rather than a synonym: something travellers take

blocks.note: the main is an old word for the open sea
a passage is a section of text

explanation.surface: Travellers carry off the central section of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: Main reads as most important, but here it is the poetic name for the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Voyagers book a crossing by ship, a journey over the ocean.

clue.text: List of courses for chaps at university

blocks.note: chaps are men
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A prospectus of courses for male students at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: Courses suggests academic study, but these are courses of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant card sets out the dishes served, starter through dessert.

clue.text: Blocking - the road?

blocks.note: first meaning: obstructing
second meaning, read literally: located on the way, since a way is a road

explanation.surface: Something obstructing the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal reading: a way is a road, so something in the way is on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstruction stands where it hinders passage, and literally a way is a route.

clue.text: Bound to be performed by the ballet dancer

definitions.text: Bound to be performed by the ballet dancer

blocks.clueFragment: Bound to be performed by the ballet dancer
blocks.note: surface reading: something the dancer is obliged to do

blocks.clueFragment: Bound to be performed by the ballet dancer
blocks.note: setter's reading: a particular leap a ballet dancer performs

explanation.surface: A ballet dancer will certainly have to perform something.
explanation.walkthrough: Bound looks like 'certain to', but it is a noun meaning a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: In ballet this is a jump in which the dancer crosses the feet rapidly while in the air.

clue.text: She is a beautiful Italian

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
bella is the Italian word for beautiful

explanation.surface: Praise for a lovely Italian woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Beautiful Italian means the Italian for beautiful, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: She stands for any woman, and this is a female first name.

clue.text: Father returns with skiers out for social activity

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read in the opposite direction
out suggests being disordered or put awry, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: pa is a familiar word for father
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Dad comes back with the skiers who have been out on the slopes, ready for a night of fun.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the French term for the socialising in bars and lodges after a day on the slopes.

clue.text: Change the course of a revolution

blocks.note: first meaning: to steer something in a new direction
second meaning: one full rotation

explanation.surface: Altering the direction of a political uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolution suggests an uprising, but here it is a spin of a wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to alter direction, and the noun means a single rotation.

clue.text: Understand it's describing figures below ten

blocks.note: dig is slang for understand or appreciate
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Grasping that something describes small numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: The single numerals zero to nine are each a digit, so these are the figures under ten.

clue.text: A staged production

blocks.note: surface reading: a play put on in a theatre
setter's reading: factory manufacture done in stages along a conveyor

explanation.walkthrough: Staged suggests the theatre, but it means carried out in successive stages.
explanation.definitionFit: In a factory, workers each add one step as goods move past them on a conveyor belt.

clue.text: Record a stage direction

blocks.note: first meaning: to write into a log or register
second meaning: the script instruction for an actor to come on

explanation.surface: Writing down an instruction in a play script.
explanation.definitionFit: Data is entered in a ledger, and a script marks an actor's arrival onstage with this word.

clue.text: Young fishwife who survived Henry VIII

blocks.note: first meaning: a young salmon
surface only: the word must be split after its first four letters to separate the two meanings
second meaning: Catherine, the sixth and last wife of the Tudor king

explanation.walkthrough: Fishwife runs the two definitions together; split after fish. Catherine Parr outlived Henry VIII.
explanation.definitionFit: A parr is a juvenile salmon, and Catherine Parr was the queen still married to Henry when he died.

clue.text: Possibly meant to join number around the fire

definitions.note: a description: the frame surrounding a fireplace

indicators.note: joining puts one thing beside another, so the pieces are set side by side
possibly suggests one arrangement out of several, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Perhaps intended to gather a crowd round the fireside.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantelpiece is the ornamental shelf and frame surrounding a hearth.

clue.text: Pat his arm in error

indicators.note: in error means wrongly placed, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone pats another's arm by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: Pat looks like a verb, but it is a name: Pat (Patrick) is a traditional nickname for a man from Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Pat, short for Patrick after the patron saint, is a stock name for a man from Ireland.

clue.text: He'll bear out it's a drinking place

indicators.note: bearing something out here means setting the letters out in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone will confirm that a certain spot is a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A large tavern where beer is served, typical of Bavaria, is a venue for drinking.

clue.text: It joins in operations

blocks.note: surface reading: something that takes part in campaigns or business activity
setter's reading: the stitch a surgeon uses to close a wound

explanation.surface: Something that takes part in activities.
explanation.walkthrough: Joins in looks like 'takes part', but it means sews together, and operations are surgical.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon's stitch closes the edges of an incision or wound.
